fit: oregano essential oil and rotarod in healthy rats
assessment: Rotating-rod retention was inconclusive and high-dose males showed more exploration. Neither result measures stride length after fresh oregano in Parkinson’s.

fit: oral canola oil and a paced tapping imaging task
assessment: Motor BOLD decreased after canola oil during instructed tapping. No separate tapping-performance result, refined-oil confirmation or Parkinson sample.

fit: canola crossover and monitored paced finger-tapping rate
assessment: Tapping was 2.09 ± 0.27 Hz SEM across trials with no significant variation at the paced target. Speeded dexterity or accuracy and refining were unverified.

fit: Crisco canola hand-arthritis comparator with invalid grip measurements
assessment: Grip data were discarded because the instrument failed. Product composition was reported without confirmed processing or a dexterity result.

fit: mixed thyme tablet and patient urgency intensity
assessment: Urgency intensity changed from 1.357 to 1.26 with p=.705. The uncontrolled mix does not separate fresh thyme, urgency frequency or Parkinson outcomes.

fit: Thymus vulgaris oil in a multi-oil cystitis comparison
assessment: The original abstract records void frequency after eight oils, with no separate urgency outcome or fresh thyme comparison.

fit: oral isolated thymoquinone and open-field movement in rotenone mice
assessment: A single-agent group moved farther and faster. Beam and hanging-wire outcomes were inconclusive, with three animals per arm and no ground seed comparison.

fit: hydroalcoholic nigella seed extract and haloperidol catalepsy
assessment: Neither single-plant extract dose showed a significant catalepsy contrast. The mixture was not separately tested for a motor effect.

fit: isolated thymoquinone and chlorpromazine motor tests
assessment: The original abstract reports favorable catalepsy and locomotion comparisons in rats. It gives no ground culinary seed or Parkinson bradykinesia result.

fit: commercial cardamom food essence used as a sniffed smell-test item
assessment: Correct identification occurred in 36 of 87 Parkinson cases and 49 of 58 controls. This is an assessment stimulus with no ground cardamom ingestion contrast.

fit: cardamom essence in an endocrine smell identification test
assessment: Cardamom was one of ten fixed diagnostic odors. Cross-sectional score differences do not test oral cardamom or Parkinson olfactory change.
Some early attention estimates favored the extract in healthy adults. Species, formulation and clinical population differ from ground green cardamom in Parkinson’s.

fit: oral chili and an observed brief syncopal event
assessment: The original confirms seated syncope after mole poblano without falling to the floor. Systolic pressure and pulse were lower at the nearest half-hour reading. Ground-cayenne exposure and Parkinson fall frequency were unverified.

fit: oral chili challenge and measured hypotension and bradycardia
assessment: Challenge reproduced a marked pressure and pulse decrease. The discussion calls the pepper cayenne without verifying the preparation. No measured falls or Parkinson cohort.

fit: pooled spinach and leek intake in a Parkinson cohort
assessment: The weekly intake category pools both vegetables and reports no raw spinach or dyskinesia effect estimate.

fit: oral safflower comparison in a progressive supranuclear palsy trial
assessment: US registry names safflower and the EU record lists global study end. No pressing method, fall count or posted comparative results.

fit: asparagus oral liquid with mecobalamin and reported unstimulated saliva
assessment: A later systematic review extracts a positive salivary-flow comparison in 28 burning-mouth patients with high risk of bias. The original body is unavailable, and drooling, steamed food and Parkinson effects are unverified.

fit: pooled leek and spinach intake in a Parkinson cohort
assessment: The single weekly leafy-green category cannot identify roasted leek or estimate effects on clinical rigidity.
